hero.h1: Owning good technology should never be a gamble.
hero.lede: Mode 7 is a technology hub built on one observation — that buying a device, powering it and upgrading it are separate problems, and almost nobody solves them together.

second.h: A device is only as good as everything standing behind it.
second.lede: Every unit carrying our name is sourced, inspected, sealed and warrantied by us.

image.alt: A technician in white gloves polishing a smartphone at an inspection bench, with precision screwdrivers, a loupe, tweezers and cleaning supplies laid out around them.

why.h2: We didn’t set out to open another storefront.
paragraphs: We set out to close a gap. Someone saves for months, buys a flagship device from a seller they cannot verify, and finds out too late that the box was opened, the warranty is fiction, or the battery has already been replaced once. The device is genuine or it isn’t — and there is rarely a way to know before the money moves.

So we built the opposite of that. Every unit carrying our name is sourced, inspected, sealed and warrantied by us. When it later needs power or replacing, those answers come from the same place. We sell the way people actually buy here, too — in conversation, questions answered before money moves, rather than a form bolted on top of a habit that was never going to change.
why.statement: A device is only as good as everything standing behind it.

serve.h2: Three people walk in with three different problems.
serve.lede: The catalogue is the same. What changes is the question being asked of it — and the part of the ecosystem that ends up answering.

items.b: People whose income depends on the device in their hand. It has to be genuine, it has to arrive quickly, and it has to keep working through a day that doesn't pause.
Homes built up in stages — a room, a system, a season at a time. Lighting and power first, comfort next, without being forced to commit to one ecosystem on day one.
Teams equipping staff at volume — consolidated invoicing, a named account manager, and a refresh cycle that can actually be planned against a budget.

conditions.h2: Every part of this business answers something specific.
conditions.lede: We are not a general-purpose retailer that happens to operate here. These four conditions shape the market we serve — and each one is the reason a particular part of Mode 7 exists.

items.b: Grid supply is intermittent, and planning around it is ordinary life rather than an emergency. A device is only as useful as the energy behind it — which is why panels, inverters and batteries sit in our catalogue beside the laptops, not in a separate business.

Grey imports. Refurbished units sold as new. Warranties that evaporate on first contact. "Sealed" is a claim most of this market cannot actually back, so we made verification a documented process with a paper trail — and only then started using the word.

A flagship device can cost several months of earnings. Certified refurbished is not a lesser tier for people who cannot afford better — for most buyers it is the difference between having the tool and going without it entirely.

The phone in your hand or the laptop on your desk is frequently the business itself. Downtime is lost income, not inconvenience. That turns upgrade paths and trade-in liquidity into commercial questions that deserve commercial answers.

bento.lede: Each of these five divisions answers one of the conditions described above — an unreliable grid, trust that has to be rebuilt, hardware priced against income, or a device that doubles as someone's livelihood. What ties them together is the same standard: sourced, verified, powered and renewed against one set of rules, so the guarantee behind the sale doesn't change with the category.

divisions.b: Flagship phones, business laptops and pro tablets across thirteen brands. Genuine, factory-sealed, inspected before dispatch, and covered by the manufacturer's warranty as well as ours.

image.alt: An iMac, MacBook, iPhone and keyboard arranged together on a desk — the flagship phones, laptops and tablets Mode 7 carries.

divisions.b: Renewed, graded and sealed again — a fifty-point inspection, a twelve-month warranty, and the exact grade published before you buy rather than discovered after.
Panels, inverters, home batteries and portable power. Sized against real consumption — so everything else in the catalogue keeps working when the grid doesn't.
Lighting, climate and security as compatible kits you start small and extend — never a whole-house commitment made in one go.
A valuation in about a minute, applied instantly against anything in store. Capital sitting idle inside an old device becomes the deposit on the next one, without a negotiation.

spec.h2: Three words, and what they oblige us to.
spec.lede: They only mean anything if one party is willing to stand behind all three. So we publish what each one commits us to, and apply it to every unit we sell.
bar: Applies to every unit · new and renewed

words.d: Inspected against a published checklist before it is allowed into stock — not spot-checked at the door.
Closed under our own tamper tape, so the state it left us in is the state it reaches you in.
Warrantied by us, not only by the manufacturer. One party to call, whichever part failed.

mission.label: Mission
mission.body: Sourced, verified, powered and renewed against a single standard — so that owning it is never a risk the buyer carries alone.

vision.label: Vision
vision.statement: A market where trust is the default, not the exception.
vision.body: Every device with a verifiable history. Every home in control of its own power. Upgrading decided by what you need — never by whether the seller can be believed.

stats: Sealed and warrantied — new or renewed
